scientific_scope_status: Two passive systems can have identical accessible scattering and total-loss flags but exchange target/parasitic sink labels, so even adaptive external control cannot infer the hidden sink from that interface. A passive one-port resonator can reduce total loss while a new target sink absorbs positive energy. The positive finite-power saturable-bucket theorem is stated for 0<a<b and requires (ab)^(1/3)(a^(1/3)+b^(1/3))<=1, along with fixed delivered target-plane power, full complex control, complete energy collection, a qualified single-pass homogeneous saturable absorber, acquired response and reset. Nonlinear bucket and iTRAN methods are strong incumbents; no new demonstrated capability or practical advantage follows.
